reason: The idea survives the value/transfer lens as private-rank insurance. It is not a score idea. (1) No in-sample lab number carries it. The inputs are the LB insertion replicates (#27->#28 and #34->#35, +0.001 each) and a prior on lowrefine. (2) It is not a node-count artefact: the insertion is the last edit and adds no nodes (RESULTS #35 / exp57b), so the twin's node rows equal K2's. (3) It is not a closed line: nothing is tuned on public. Metric ceilings: the private effect of the insertion is at most ~0.002 (0.1 x dJ_div plus a few edges; public J ~0.36 from safe-div off 0.911 vs 0.947). Lowrefine is ~1e-4 to 3e-4 (1,365 readmits; one FN->TP is ~1e-5 on ~100 hidden clips). So F1 = I+L falls below X almost only when the insertion is negative on private. That has real probability because there are few evaluable events (Binomial P(I<0) ~0.1-0.25, about the idea's 0.16), even though private break-even precision (~0.1-0.2) is below public's 0.265. Our kernels are byte-deterministic, so exact copies of x138 tie at X. Any nonzero L breaks the tie, and the cliff logic holds (0.953 block at ranks 193-448, bronze ~390). My MC (scratchpad twin_mc.py, 2M draws) adds the comparator the idea left implicit: #35 (= x138+I). It is already scored, its private score already exists, and it costs no slot. Results as P(max>X), with F1 = K2 = I+L: exp52 0.876, #35 0.888, twin 0.930. With a riskier insertion: 0.726 / 0.720 / 0.877. With F1 = I+L+M: 0.924 / 0.941 / 0.950. The twin beats exp52 in every scenario. It beats #35 unless the insertion is safe on private, where it is 0.002-0.015 worse on P(>X) and ~0.02 worse on silver. Nothing states that public and private are different embryos (the split is 29/71% of the test data), which somewhat favours the safe-I world. Caveats: the twin's own P(>X) is just P(L(+M)>0), about 0.6-0.8. Its public score (3 decimals, expected 0.953, rank hidden behind our 0.954) cannot confirm L>0, so the admission rule only catches failures. The claimed +0.03 vs exp52 is right under the model, but the real increment over the best free option (#35) is ~+0.01 to +0.04 P(bronze), and 0 on silver.
fix: (a) Build the twin as K2 minus the insertion only: the K2 build with DIVINS disabled (the parity pass shows DIVINS_ENABLE=0 is byte-identical to no patch), or the existing exp58n command, which is equivalent. Then {K2, twin} differ only by I. Gate: twin node rows == K2 dummy, and edges differ only at K2's inserted forks. (b) Rewrite §f's F2 rule with three candidates, twin vs #35 vs exp52, and pre-register the order before scores: twin by default (it hedges the high-magnitude component I), #35 only if the exp60 lab or K2 vs #35 shows lowrefine risk, exp52 last (dominated). Keep 'never tick two files with identical components'. (c) Use S3 only if nothing else needs the 26 Sep spare. Otherwise use S9/S10 on 27 Sep; the value does not depend on the date. (d) If forkmid enters F1, rebuild the twin as F1 minus I (exp59n), as proposed.
realistic_gain: 0 on public and ~0 in expected private score. In P(private > raw x138 = bronze/no-medal cliff): +0.03 to +0.05 vs the plan's exp52 default in base cases (up to +0.15 if the insertion is riskier on private), but only ~+0.01 to +0.04 vs the free alternative #35. Slightly negative (-0.002 to -0.015) if the insertion is robustly positive on private. Silver-line gain ~0. Cost: one spare slot, 0.5-1 h of work, ~0.5 GPU-h dummy.
